'''Joan Carol Warnow-Blewett''' (née Nelson) (December 11, 1931 – May 30, 2006)<ref name=TandyJWarnow-FamilyHistoryPage>{{cite web|title=Family|url=http://www.cs.utexas.edu/~tandy/family.html|website=Tandy J. Warnow|accessdate=3 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501103313/http://www.cs.utexas.edu/~tandy/family.html|archive-date=1 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> was an American [[archivist]] and staff member of the [[American Institute of Physics|American Institute of Physics (AIP)]] for 32 years.<ref name=AIP-History-2008>{{cite web|title=History That Matters: Joan Warnow-Blewett|url=http://www.aip.org/history/historymatters/warnow.htm|website=[[American Institute of Physics]]|accessdate=4 August 2016|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202204155/http://www.aip.org/history/historymatters/warnow.htm|archivedate=2 December 2008}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Warnow-Blewett was born to parents David Nelson and Edith Nelson (née Sjölander), American immigrants who were born in [[Sweden]].<ref name=Sjolander-Mother-Memorial-2006>{{cite web|last1=Sjölander|first1=Kimmen|title=Joan Nelson Warnow Blewett (1931–2006) – PhyloFacts|url=http://phylogenomics.berkeley.edu/kimmen/mormor|website=Phylogenomics at Berkeley|accessdate=4 August 2016|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402062944/http://phylogenomics.berkeley.edu/kimmen/mormor|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1965, Warnow-Blewett was hired at [[American Institute of Physics|American Institute of Physics (AIP)]] as Librarian of the Niels Bohr Library. In 1974, she was promoted to Associate Director for the Center for History of Physics.<ref name=STAMAMailingList-Retirement-1997>{{cite web|last1=Anderson|first1=Joe|title=Joan Warnow-Blewett Retires|url=http://www.asap.unimelb.edu.au/asa/stama/mail/msg00173.html|website=Science, Technology and Medicine Archives (STAMA) Mailing List|publisher=Australian Society of Archivists|accessdate=3 August 2016|date=12 December 1997}}</ref>

From 1986 to 1989, she was a council member of the [[Society of American Archivists]].<ref name=SAALeadership-WarnowBlewett>{{cite web|title=History of SAA Leadership: Joan Warnow-Blewett 1986–89, American Institute of Physics|url=http://www2.archivists.org/history/leaders/council-members#.V6Kq65MrLXG|website=[[Society of American Archivists]]|accessdate=2 August 2016}}</ref>

== Contribution to scientific collaboration ==
Warnow-Blewett's work was a significant influence on the book, ''Structures of Scientific Collaboration'' by Wesley Shrum, Joel Genuth and Ivan Chompalov.<ref name=StructuresScientificCollaboration-2007>{{cite book|last1=Shrum|first1=Wesley|last2=Genuth|first2=Joel|last3=Chompalov|first3=Ivan|title=Structures of Scientific Collaboration|date=2007|publisher=MIT Press|location=Cambridge, Mass.|isbn=978-0-26-219559-1|pages=ix, 13|oclc=876555722}}</ref>

Starting in 1989, she assembled a multi-disciplinary team including social sciences, history and archives. This team collected data on 60 scientific collaborations over the span of a decade. They coded the interviews with the collaborative teams in order to create a massive database covering themes such as "invention and practice; and issues of specialization, decision-making, values, subcontracting, instrumentation, funding and, of course, credit allocation."<ref name="AmericanScientist-StudyingBigScience-2008">{{cite journal|last1=Hoddeson|first1=Lillian|date=March 2008|title=Studying Big Science|url=https://www.americanscientist.org/article/studying-big-science|journal=[[American Scientist]]|volume=96|issue=2|page=168|doi=10.1511/2008.70.168 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Warnow-Blewett was married three times. Her first marriage, which was until 1964, was to inventor Morton Warnow, with whom she had three children.<ref name=NYTimes-MortonWarnow-Obit-2006>{{cite news|title=Morton Charles Warnow: Obituary|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?page=lifestory&pid=16999517|accessdate=4 August 2016|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=8 March 2006}}</ref> In 1983, she married physicist John Paul Blewett<ref name=FamilySearch-CAMarriageIndex-1983>{{cite web|title=Joan Nelson mentioned in the record of John P Blewett and Joan Nelson|url=https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:V6JH-YQS|website=[[FamilySearch]]|accessdate=4 August 2016|date=8 June 1983}}</ref> and was married to Blewett until his death in 2000.<ref name=NYTimes-JohnPaulBlewett-Obit-2000>{{cite news|last1=Saxon|first1=Wolfgang|title=John Paul Blewett, 89, Physicist And Designer of Accelerators|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/04/19/nyregion/john-paul-blewett-89-physicist-and-designer-of-accelerators.html|accessdate=4 August 2016|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=19 April 2000}}</ref> Her third marriage was to physics historian, Martin Klein.<ref name=TandyJWarnow-FamilyHistoryPage /> She had three children: Paul Warnow, [[Kimmen Sjolander]], and [[Tandy Warnow]].<ref name="TandyJWarnow-FamilyHistoryPage" />

Warnow-Blewett died in [[Alamo, California|Alamo]], California, on May 30, 2006.<ref name=TandyJWarnow-FamilyHistoryPage /><ref name=FamilySearch-US-SSDI-2006>{{cite web|title=Joan N Blewett United States Social Security Death Index|url=https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:JGFZ-Q4W|website=[[FamilySearch]]|accessdate=4 August 2016|date=30 May 2006}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
Between 1970 and 2001, Warnow-Blewett published 60 works in 105 publications. She continued to publish after her retirement from the AIP in August 1997.<ref name=OCLC-WorldCatIdentities>{{cite web|title=Warnow-Blewett, Joan 1931–|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n79039180/|website=WorldCat Identities|publisher=[[OCLC]]|accessdate=4 August 2016}}</ref>

Final Report Documenting Multi-Institutional Collaborations|date=2001|publisher=Center for History of Physics, [[American Institute of Physics]]|location=College Park, Maryland|oclc=47204030}}<ref name=AIP-History-StudyMultiInstCollabs>{{cite web|title=Study of Multi-Institutional Collaborations|url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/study-multi-institutional-collaborations|website=[[American Institute of Physics]]|accessdate=4 August 2016}}</ref>
* {{cite book|last1=Warnow-Blewett|first1=Joan|last2=Teichmann|first2=Jürgen|title=Guide to Sources for History of Solid State Physics, Report No. 6|date=1992|publisher=Center for History of Physics, [[American Institute of Physics]]|location=New York|isbn=978-1-56-396068-0|oclc=27761357}}
